scope: React app catalog witnesses from the reference worktree; deduplicated by id across REACT_ALIGNMENT_FAMILIES and both axes.

coverage.externalLayoutBoundary: ApplicationLayout, ContentLayout and ViewLayout are deliberately runtime-excluded. Their slot allocation remains an external layout boundary; explicit gap-token dependencies are retained in extra-app-layout-boundary, and ContentLayout delegates to the included reusable grid primitive.

taxonomyPressure: Continuation is a candidate marker-led inline contract: SideNavigation and FileTree own canvas/gap and inset relationships. Test whether the entry inset is an independent semantic bucket or a composition of existing contracts before assigning a category count.

Editors contain distinct owners: toolbar actions are block-derived square controls and view tabs are bordered rows; bordered editor content has local H8/V6 outside inset, while the borderless textarea retains measured native padding2 on all four edges. Neither is automatically an accepted Surface or zero-inset contract.

Code rows are not one row token: GitDiff frame is border-only (zero padding); FileHeader is an attached row; gutter/content cells own legacy local offsets; table rows themselves are occupied-block boundaries.

Depth zero retains an empty indentation part and cancels the otherwise-owned marker gap. The visible layout box intentionally has zero inline size; this capture policy permits that one named case without treating hidden targets as measured. This is a derived mode, not another inset.

The sticky pseudo-element pulls its canvas back over the separately recorded final-list clearance. Equal positive size and negative margin are a compensation mechanism; they do not establish two vertical gaps.

The root flex column separates Header, Content and Footer. The already inventoried NavTree and group gaps are different owners and do not cover this relationship.
The table owns cell separation independently of the cell padding and gutter border. Capture borderSpacing and used cell positions before classifying its one-stroke inline separation.
